bullets.title: SNDK Investor Day: 50% FCF margin, $93.9B backlog, Meta joins HBF consortium
bullets.body: SanDisk CEO guided mid-to-high teens revenue growth and ~80% non-GAAP gross margins through FY2028-2030, with adj. FCF margins of 50% by that window. The company disclosed $93.9B in total contract value across 8 customers and plans to return 100% of excess cash to shareholders. Separately, Meta is joining a SanDisk-led consortium to develop an open standard for high-bandwidth flash; SNDK has already taped out its first HBF die. Analyst commentary flagged conservative signed NVM RPO calculation methodology as a source of upside. Wide bid/ask spreads noted today as HFTs exploit the spread.

bullets.title: NVDA: Spectrum-X photonics in full production; A100 lifecycle extended to 2029; Rubin Ultra HBM4E detail
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet photonics entered full production for gigawatt-scale AI factory networking. CEO Jensen Huang confirmed A100 GPUs remain mission-capable through 2029 (9-year lifecycle). Separately, Aletheia reports Rubin Ultra will use 8-high/12-high HBM4E (not HBM4), and the four-die configuration for Kyber remains on roadmap. CoreWeave is renting A100s through 2029, defying typical deprecation curves.

bullets.title: AMD: $5B debt offering to fund AI expansion; UBS sees Intel foundry deal; unusual 1DTE call buying
bullets.body: AMD plans to raise up to $5B via a four-part bond sale—potentially its largest ever—to fund AI capacity ramp following major deals with Anthropic and Microsoft. UBS sees AMD eventually striking a foundry partnership with Intel given its underdog status in the data center rack market. Additionally, $2M+ in 1DTE call options on NVDA and AMD were flagged as unusual activity.

bullets.title: INTC: CEO buys $12-13M in recent offering; memory reentry hints; analyst coverage inflects bullish
bullets.body: Intel's CEO purchased $12-13M of stock in a recent offering per SEC 8-K, signaling insider confidence. Intel reportedly hinted at reentry into the memory business. Analyst coverage has shifted dramatically: from 9 buys / 23 holds / 12 sells in 2023 to 19 buys / 33 holds / 2 sells in 2026, with the stock at $106 consensus PT and outperforming NVDA since early 2024. In Q2, Intel lost server CPU unit share but gained revenue share. Separately, millions in far OTM INTC calls hit the tape today.

bullets.title: CSCO: Earnings miss sends stock down >10%; AI spending reaching enterprise but mixed signal
bullets.body: Cisco's Q2 earnings miss led to a >10% stock decline, per the daily semiconductor/AI infrastructure update. Commentary noted AI spending is reaching enterprise hardware but adoption signals remain mixed compared to hyperscaler-level buildouts.

bullets.title: MU: $707 seen as the low; $2.7M call at $2,000 strike; semis recover half their losses
bullets.body: One analyst argues MU at $707 was the cycle bottom, framing HBM and DRAM as non-commodity, high-margin data center products. Separately, a $2.7M call order at the $2,000 strike (109% OTM) appeared, described as a major speculative bullish bet. The broader semiconductor ETF (SMH) has recovered roughly half of June/July losses. Earlier in the week, NVDA/AMD/MU call positions reportedly doubled as the sector rallied.

bullets.title: CIEN / NOK: AI campus scale trend seen as structural tailwind; COHR confirms supply chain clarity
bullets.body: An analyst argues CIEN and NOK stand to benefit from AI campus scale-across trends flagged in LITE and COHR Q4 guidance. COHR's Q4 call confirmed that transceiver assembly is not the primary supply chain bottleneck, clarifying concerns. Silicon germanium capacity at GlobalFoundries is oversubscribed due to 200G/400G optics demand for TIAs.

bullets.title: NFLX: Bill Ackman re-enters with new position; Pershing Square largest portfolio revamp in years
bullets.body: Bill Ackman disclosed a new Netflix position as part of his largest portfolio overhaul in years. Pershing Square's Q2 additions include Netflix alongside Visa, Mastercard, and others. Ackman expects strong earnings growth to drive long-term value; Pershing Square is down 3.5% YTD through July vs. S&P 500's 13% gain.

bullets.title: IREN delivers Horizon 1 to MSFT; achieves NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on GB300
bullets.body: IREN announced it delivered its Horizon 1 product to Microsoft and achieved NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on the GB300 platform. MSFT also cut carbon removal credit purchases by ~80% YoY (8.55M metric tons vs prior year) to prioritize AI spending.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 3.7 Flash launched for coding/agents; NVDA hyperscaler dynamic intensifying
bullets.body: Google launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, described as its most intelligent workhorse model for coding and agents. One analyst note outlines NVDA's strategy to commoditize the data center layer while hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL) attack the chip design layer; neocloud business models are affected by NVDA revenue share arrangements.

bullets.title: SMCI: Earnings-day buyer holds; smuggling scandal and $65-72B FY27 guidance vs $25B market cap scrutinized
bullets.body: One trader bought SMCI on earnings day after reviewing guidance and sees recent weakness as overdone. A bearish take flags SMCI's alleged smuggling of NVDA GPUs and questions whether $65-72B FY2027 revenue guidance is credible against a ~$25B market cap, contrasting the company unfavorably with DELL.

bullets.title: IONQ / RGTI / QBTS: Q2 quantum earnings reviewed; thesis intact, now a stock-picker's market
bullets.body: All five U.S. quantum pure-plays reported Q2. The quantum thesis survived but the trade has shifted from a basket approach to individual stock selection. IONQ is cited by one user as 'in the strongest position to dominate in coming years.' Government spending is accelerating and Q2 revenue/guidance trends were up.

bullets.title: AAPL: Trader buys pre-iPhone event calls targeting all-time highs
bullets.body: A trader disclosed buying AAPL $315 calls at $4 and $325 calls at $1.70, both expiring 9/11, as a directional bet on a run-up into the upcoming iPhone launch event, with intent to exit before the event itself.

bullets.title: AMZN: Sales desk signals buy at open; Pershing Square holds position
bullets.body: One trader signaled buying AMZN at the open and discussing bullish/bearish single-stock views. Bill Ackman's Pershing Square also held AMZN among Q2 disclosed positions alongside UBER, MSFT, and META.

bullets.title: 30Y Treasury auction at highest yield since 2001: 5.216%; macro rate regime matters for tech
bullets.body: The 30-year bond auction cleared at 5.216% with a 0.4bps tail—the highest yield since 2001. Bid-to-cover was 2.39x; indirect bidders took 66.8%. BofA economists separately forecast 3 Fed rate hikes in 2026, while CreditSights sees rates unchanged through H1 2027. Fed speakers Barkin and Hammack both kept rate hikes on the table but showed no urgency post soft PPI.

bullets.title: PPI cooler than expected in July; S&P 500 hits all-time high at 7,800
bullets.body: July PPI came in flat at 0.0% M/M vs +0.2% estimate (YoY +4.7% vs +4.9% est); core PPI +0.2% vs +0.3% est. The soft print drove rate-hike probability sharply lower. The S&P 500 crossed 7,800 for the first time (9th 100-point milestone of the year) and the VIX plunged below 15 to 2026 lows. Equal-weight RSP also hit all-time highs, signaling market breadth.

bullets.title: Tech guidance raises running at 2.3x historical average this earnings season
bullets.body: Nearly one-third of tech stocks that reported earnings this season raised guidance—2.3x the 25-year historical average of 14%. Health Care, Real Estate, and Industrials are also raising guidance at double historical rates, suggesting broad corporate optimism.

bullets.title: TSLA: Swedish union suspends industrial action as of Aug 19; self-inflicted issues cited by former bull
bullets.body: Swedish union IF Metall will suspend its industrial action against Tesla starting August 19, removing a labor headwind. A former Tesla bull (2019-2023, cautious since 2024) argues most of TSLA's current challenges are self-inflicted and fixable with marketing investment, but holds no current position.

bullets.title: NBIS/NVDA: Nebius deploys NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure with Vantage Data Centers in Wales
bullets.body: Nebius secured a commercial capacity commitment with Vantage Data Centers to deploy high-density NVIDIA-powered AI infrastructure at the CWL1 campus in Newport, Wales—its first announced commercial capacity commitment in the South Wales AI Growth zone.
